inputs.question: What obligations does the EU AI Act place on providers of general-purpose AI models, when do they apply, and which major AI companies signed the 2025 GPAI Code of Practice (and which refused)?

metadata.origin: live run 01M79SGHX1E1TA268VS4X1S29S missed the refusal part

outputs.answer: Article 53: every GPAI provider must keep technical documentation for the AI Office (Annex XI), give information to downstream providers (Annex XII), have a policy to comply with EU copyright law, and publish a summary of training content; open-source models are exempt from the two documentation duties unless they carry systemic risk. Article 55: models with systemic risk (presumed above 10^25 FLOPs of training compute, or designated by the Commission) must also run model evaluations including adversarial testing, assess and mitigate systemic risks, report serious incidents, and ensure cybersecurity. The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024; GPAI obligations apply from 2 August 2025; models placed on the market before then must comply by 2 August 2027; the Commission's enforcement powers (fines) apply from 2 August 2026. The Code of Practice was published on 10 July 2025. Signatories include Amazon, Anthropic, Google, IBM, Microsoft, Mistral AI, OpenAI, Aleph Alpha and Cohere; xAI signed only the Safety and Security chapter. Meta publicly refused to sign.
required_parts: Article 53 obligations for all GPAI providers
Article 55 extra obligations for systemic-risk models
Application dates: 2 August 2025, and 2 August 2027 for models already on the market
Companies that signed the Code of Practice
